findings.finding: The Jan-2027 price cap is forecast to rise 21-27% on the Iran war and Hormuz gas spike. In FY26 the company blamed its churn rise to 14.2% on a wholesale forward curve that let competitors sell fixed tariffs well below the cap. A rising curve removes that, and the E.ON contract insulates TEP's margin, so H2 commentary on churn and customer growth should lean positive. The offset is higher bad-debt risk (FY26 bad debt 2.1% of sales and rising), which the company says is recovered through the cap allowance.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Customer-momentum updates rose: AGM statement +5.96% (2026-08-17) and the Oct trading update about +2% on the day (825 to 843p). The FY26 results with the churn rise and guide cut fell 25.7%.
findings.why_not_priced: The cap forecast moved sharply only in mid-to-late November (Cornwall Insight's +26% on 18 Nov). The stock fell from 945p (4-5 Nov) to about 870p over the same weeks, which is not what a market pricing a churn tailwind would do. The company has not yet commented on the Jan cap's effect on competition. The read is still macro-to-company transmission, so it is sized small.
findings.independence: https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/great-britain-energy-bills-rise-january-2027-forecast-1833134 (18 Nov 2026, Cornwall Insight +26%) and https://www.uswitch.com/gas-electricity/news/energy-price-cap-january-2027-latest-predictions-and-news/ (updated 23 Nov 2026, +27% supplier average). These confirm the curve move, not the effect on TEP.

findings.finding: H1 adjusted PBT will be about 15% of the £80-90m guide (about £12-13.5m, my arithmetic) against an H1 FY26 of about a quarter of £132m. The wire headline will read as a profit collapse, but the company has pre-signalled it three times.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The H1 FY26 results (25 Nov 2025: profit down, guide reiterated) fell 5.74%. H1 FY25 rose 2.16%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the 15/85 phasing has been stated since 23 June and repeated on 17 Aug and 6 Oct. The only unpriced part is retail reaction to the headline on a retail-heavy register.

findings.finding: The interim distribution follows a disclosed formula: 40% of FY27 distributions (c.80% of adjusted PAT), half as dividend and half as a buyback extension. That implies an interim dividend of about 13p (my arithmetic) against 38p last year, and a buyback extension of about £10m with roughly £4-9m of the £40m programme left.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The dividend reset announced with the FY26 final (12p final) came on the day of the 25.7% fall, which mixed it with the guide cut. No clean history.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. The formula and split are public and the 12p final already reset the run-rate. A yield-screen headline (interim down about 65%) is the residual risk, partly offset by an extended buyback at about 870p, below the c.900p VWAPs of the last fortnight.

outside_window.finding: Ofgem announces the 1 Jan - 31 Mar 2027 price cap on 25 Nov 2026, the day after the exit window. Forecasts are +21-27%.

lessons_applied: 'A finding about a number the market has already been told is worth 0': the H1 PBT finding moved from -0.3 to -0.1 and the interim distribution finding from -0.2 to -0.1. Both lines were pre-released on 6 Oct.

'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series / macro-to-company transmission is a hypothesis': the energy-curve finding moved from +0.6 to +0.5. It is kept because the company itself tied churn to the forward-curve shape.

'The move is in the guide': with the guide likely reiterated and the period pre-released, abs_move moved from 4.5 to 4.0, still above the 3% base because of the name's own 3.8% median and thin coverage.
